contexts.text: The brazen serpent = the Lord's Sensuous, who... alone is circumspect and provides for all.
To provide that he could not enter into any arcanum of faith. Signified.
Of the Lord's Providence...
The Lord foresees, provides, and disposes everything; but some things from permission; some from admission; some from leave; some from good pleasure; and some from will.
He provides and disposes that evils are turned into goods.
Providence not merely universal.
He provides that goods are never mixed with evils.
The Lord's Providence takes care that man is not admitted further into faith of heart than he can be kept in it.
He provides that no one has more truth than he receives of good.
The least things are foreseen and provided to eternity. AC 2694.
Attribute all things to prudence, and little or nothing to the Divine Providence.
The Divine Providence is universal because in the most singular things... AC 3175:4.
Acknowledge a universal Providence, which is none.
The Lord's Providence preventing man from entering from himself into the mysteries of faith. Signified.
Thought about everything... to eternity, with the Divine Providence. Signified.
Jehovah shall see = the Lord's Providence. AC 2839.
He shall send His Angel before thee = the Divine Providence. AC 3154:4.
Providence from eternity. Signified.
That all things are now provided. Signified.
The Lord as to the state of Providence. Signified.
Providence that Divine good and truth be not profaned. Explained. AC 3402:2.
Providence. Signified.
The Lord's foresight and Providence... Signified.
As the Lord foresees this, He also provides...
I will keep thee... = the Divine Providence.
A state of Providence. Signified, Explained.
Those who reason about the Divine Providence... cannot know these innumerable arcana of Providence... AC 4031:2.
Jehovah saw = the Lord's foresight and Providence.
There is foresight relatively to man; Providence relatively to the Lord...
The foresight and Providence of the Lord are in the most minute singulars with man...
Jehovah hath heard, in the supreme sense, = Providence...

The Foresight of the Lord is to see from eternity to eternity that it is so; and the Providence of the Lord is to rule so that it is so, and to bend the freedom of man to good, in so far as He foresees that man will suffer himself to be bent in freedom.
The votive sacrifices... in the internal sense, = that the Lord would provide; in the supreme, a state of Providence.
Face of eagle = circumspection and thence Providence...
Stipulated from what was provided. Signified, Explained.
The Lord's Providence is especially concerned with the conjunction of good and truth. Explained.
Foresight and Providence. Signified.
To listen to anyone, when predicated of God, = Providence.
A remnant of the Church is always provided.
To will that the Lord should provide. Signified, Explained.
To obey, when predicated of the Lord, = to provide. Explained.
Of the Lord's Divine Providence.
The Lord's presence through Foresight and Providence. Signified.
Those things which happened of the Divine Providence. Signified.
The Lord's universal Providence without the most singular things which are in it, and from which it is, is nothing at all.
Truths from the Divine Providence. Signified.
The Lord thus bends by a silent Providence...
To be with anyone in the way in which he walks, when predicated of the Lord, = His Divine Providence; for to provide is properly to be with anyone, and to protect from evils.
Simeon, in the supreme sense, = Providence.

Spirits who inflowed strongly into the thought when the things of Providence were being treated of. Example(s). They were those who when they had prayed for anything, and had not obtained it, had doubted concerning Providence.
That all things were from the Divine Providence. Signified. (See Prosper.)
That the Divine Providence is from Him. Signified.

The Lord knows everything, and provides every moment. If He were to intermit it for an instant, all the progressions would be disturbed... (Thus) the Divine Foresight and Providence is in the most singular things: if it were only universal, the human race would perish.
What was provided. Signified, Explained.

Providence is predicated of good; but Foresight of evil; for ail good inflows from the Lord, and therefore this is provided... Providence about evil is nothing else than the direction or determination of evil to a less evil, and, so far as possible, to good...
For they attribute to themselves that which is of the Divine Providence.
Fortune is the ultimate of Providence.
Providence regards the successive state to eternity...
Apperceived what was provided. Signified.

For all that the Lord does is Providence, which, being from the Divine, has in it what is eternal and infinite... This is called Providence; and as this is in everything which the Lord does, therefore His doing cannot be expressed by any other word than Providence.
States of Providence. Signified, Explained.
For what is of the Divine Providence certainly happens.
These historical things happened of Providence, that Divine things might be represented. AC 5316. AC 5620:14. AC 5688:2.
Foresight and Providence of the Celestial of the Spiritual. Signified.

God doing = Providence; for all that God does can be expressed by no other word than Providence; for the reason that in all He does there are what is eternal and what is infinite; and these are in the word Providence.
Reflection from the good of that truth upon the things hitherto provided. Signified.

For everything which happens... is from Providence. The Divine Providence operates thus invisibly and incomprehensibly, in order that man may in freedom ascribe it either to Providence, or to chance; for if Providence were to act visibly and comprehensibly there would be danger... of man's believing that it was of Providence, and afterwards going into the contrary: thus... truth would be profaned...
For prudence corresponds to Providence...
Spiritual life in them from Providence. Signified, Explained.

Such is the Lord's Providence, and indeed continuous; although man... denies Providence in singular things, when yet it is in the most singular things of all, from the first thread of man's life to... eternity. More things of Providence concur in each moment with every man than can be comprehended by any number.
Consulted for by the Divine Providence. Signified.
This was of a peculiar Divine Providence.
To provide bread () = the sustentation of spiritual life.
So done from Providence by the Divine. Signified.
Foresight and Providence to eternity. Signified.

God shall be with you = the Lord's Divine Providence... For when the Lord is with anyone, He leads him, and provides that all things which happen ... turn out for his good: this is the Divine Providence.
As... the Lord's influx through Heaven, and immediately from Himself, is more fitly called Providence therefore in what follows we may say Providence.

(Souls) take with them the opinion that the Divine Providence is (only) universal, from seeing the wicked (succeed), not knowing that the Divine Providence has for its end man's eternal salvation... AC 8717:3.
The Lord provides His ends through the evil (also).
(Argument for a particular Providence.)

One who had confirmed himself... that nothing is of the Divine Providence, but everything from prudence, fortune, and chance... It was shown that every single thing of his life had been guided by the Lord, and that he would have precipitated himself into the most frightful Hell if the least thing had ceased from the Lord's continual Providence.

The good Spirits said that man's prudence is to the Divine Providence as a mote is to the universal atmosphere... They said, further, that all contingent things are of Providence; and that Providence acts silently and secretly... SE 4393.

The Angels said that the Lord's Providence is in the most singular things of all; but not according to such an order as man proposes to himself, because the things to come are both foreseen and provided; and that it is like one building a palace, who first heaps up materials of every kind which lie without any order, while the resultant palace is solely in the understanding of the architect. AC 6487. SE 3724.
If the Lord's Providence were not in the most singular things, man could not possibly be saved, nor even live...
The sphere of ends, which is of Providence from the Lord.
That the Lord's Providence is infinite, and regards what is eternal, may be evident from the formation of embryos in the womb...

It was said, further, that the least things of all, down to the leasts of the leasts, are directed by the Lord's Providence, even as to the very steps; and that when such a sphere prevails as is contrary thereto, misfortunes happen.

What is called fortune is from the influx of Providence in the ultimates of order... Thus Providence is in the most singular things of all, according to the Lord's words, that not a hair falls from the head without the will of God. AC 6493. SE 4562.
That God will provide. Signified.
All who have firmly impressed on themselves that all things are of Own prudence, and nothing of the Divine Providence, in the other life are very prone to magic...
Providence from the Divine. Signified. (This) was predicated of the Lord as to the Human, when He was in the world.
Jehovah said = Providence.
By such an influx the Lord leads man by Providence... in the most singular things of all.
(References to passages on the subject of Providence.) NJHD 276.
Truth Divine... without successive formation inflows into the ultimates of order, and there, from the First immediately also, rules and provides each and all things.
To lead, when done by God, = Providence.
Peace has in it confidence in the Lord, that He... provides all things...
That the Lord daily provides necessaries. Signified.

The Divine Providence is universal... and those who are in the stream of Providence are continually carried to things happy... and those are in the stream of Providence who trust in the Divine, and attribute all things to Him; and those are not in the stream of Providence who trust in themselves alone, and attribute all things to themselves; for they are in the opposite, because they derogate from the Divine Providence, and claim it for themselves. It is also to be known that in proportion as anyone is in the stream of Providence, in the same proportion he is in a state of peace; and also that in proportion as anyone is in a state of peace from the good of faith, in the same proportion he is in the Divine Providence. These alone know and believe that the Lord's Divine Providence is in... the most singular things of all... and that the Divine Providence regards what is eternal.
But those in the opposite scarcely want Providence to be named...

The Divine Providence differs from all other leading and control in this: that Providence continually regards what is eternal, and continually leads to salvation, and this through various states, now glad, now sorrowful, which man cannot possibly comprehend, but still all are conducive to his life in eternity. This is signified by the journeyings at the mouth of Jehovah.
Those who in temptations almost disbelieve in the Divine Providence, Treated of.
The Divine disposition or Providence...
Few ascribe to the Divine Providence...

Therefore the Lord provides for the good who receive His mercy in time, such things as conduce to the happiness of their eternal life; riches and honours for those to whom they are not injurious, and none for those to whom they are; to the latter He gives, in time, in place of honours and riches, to be glad with a few things, and to be content more than the rich and honoured.
The Divine Providence of the Lord... which is truth Divine proceeding from His Divine good. Signified.
Such attribute all things to self... (and) wholly deny the Divine Providence in such things...
Those who were of the Ancient Churches knew that the Lord's Providence is in each and all things; and that contingent things, that is, those which appear as of chance, are of Providence...
For the Lord in every present time foresees what is evil and provides what is good.
To keep thee in the way = His Providence and guard from the falsities of evil.
Providence is to provide and look out for; thus to lead to good and guard from evil...
For everything which the Lord ordinates, that is, provides, with man and Angel, is eternal.
(The connection of man's coming to dignities and wealth with the Divine Providence.) Fully explained.

The goods and happinesses which the Lord provides for man are eternal... That which lasts to eternity is, but that which has an end relatively is not; the former is provided by the Divine, but not the latter, except in so far as it is conducive to the former. AC 10775.
All disposition into good, which is called Providence, is thence. Explained.

The government of the Lord in the Heavens and on earth is called Providence; and, as all the good of love and truth of faith are from Him, and not at all from man, it is evident that the Lord's Divine Providence is in each and all things which conduce to the salvation of the human race. Signified. AC 10774.
Those who think from worldly things about the Divine Providence conclude that it is only universal, and that the singular things are with man. (Explained.)

Nevertheless the Divine Providence continually accompanies (Own prudence), by permitting and continually withdrawing from evil. But to be led to things happy in Heaven... is effected from His Divine Providence by disposing and continually leading to good.
The Lord alone provides that there shall be equilibrium between good and evil...
On Providence. Chapter. (From AC 10773. et seq.).
The Divine Providence in reforming, regenerating, and saving men, partakes equally of the Divine love and the Divine Wisdom...
(Title). Angelic Wisdom concerning the Divine Providence.
I. That the Divine Providence is the government of the Divine love and Divine wisdom of the Lord. General article. AE 152, Signified. AE 152:end.
That it is of the Divine Providence that every created thing be such a one... Explained.
The chief end and operation of the Divine Providence is that man may be in good and at the same time in truth... and may not have a divided mind. (Explained.)
That the Lord's Divine Providence causes evil and falsity to serve for equilibrium, relation, and purification... Explained.
(Thus) it is the perpetual object of the Divine Providence, with man, to unite good to truth, and truth to good; for thus man is united to the Lord.
That the Divine Providence has for its end a Heaven from the human race. General article.
(The various subordinate ends of the Divine Providence.) Enumerated.
That the Lord's Divine Providence, in all it does, regards what is infinite and eternal. General article.

That the Divine Providence, in all it does, regards what is infinite and eternal from itself... The infinite and eternal from itself is the Divine proceeding, or the Lord in others... and this Divine is the same as the Divine Providence; for, through the Divine from Himself, the Lord provides that all things be in order... and, as the Divine proceeding operates this, it follows that the whole of it is the Divine Providence.
That to regard the infinite and eternal in forming the angelic Heaven, so as to be before the Lord as one man, which is His image, is the inmost of the Divine Providence. Explained.
This is the inmost of the Divine Providence concerning Hell.
That there are laws of the Divine Providence which are unknown to men. General article.
That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man should act from freedom according to reason. General article.

That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man, as from himself, should remove evils as sins in the external man; and that thus and no otherwise the Lord can remove evils in the internal man, and then at the same time in the external. General article.
That it is a Continual of the Divine Providence that He conjoin man with Himself and Himself with him, so that He can give him the felicities of eternal life... Explained.

Two arcana... from which can be seen the quality of the Divine Providence. One is that the Lord never acts into anything particular with man, without acting into all things together. The other is that the Lord acts from inmosts and from ultimates at the same time. Explained. DP 125.

That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man should not be compelled by external means to think and will... the things of religion; but that man should lead and sometimes compel himself. General article.

That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man should be led and taught from Heaven through the Word, doctrine, and preachings therefrom, and this in all appearance as of himself. General article.
That it is a law of the Divine Providence that man should not perceive and feel anything of the operation of the Divine Providence, but that he should still know and acknowledge it. General article.

(Arguments of the natural man against there being a Divine Providence.) DP 182. DP 216. DP 236. DP 237. DP 238. DP 249, General article. DP 250, General article. DP 251, General article. DP 252, General article. DP 254-274, General article.
That if man perceived and felt the operation of the Divine Providence, he would not act from freedom according to reason, nor would anything appear to him as his. Explained.
For the Lord through His Divine Providence leads all; and man does not lead himself except apparently.

The operation of the Lord's Divine Providence is continual to withdraw man from evils; and if anyone were to perceive and feel this continual operation... would he not continually resist it, and thus either quarrel with God, or else mix himself up with the Divine Providence...
That if man manifestly saw the Divine Providence, he would introduce himself into the order and tenor of its progression, and would pervert and destroy it. Explained.
That if man were at the same time in internal things, he would pervert and destroy all the order and tenor of the Divine Providence. Explained.
That if man manifestly saw the Divine Providence, he would either deny God, or make himself God. Explained.
For the Divine Providence never acts together with the love of man's will; but continually against it...

Hence the Lord does not manifestly appear in His Providence; but leads man by it as silently as a hidden current does a ship... (and thus) freedom appropriates to man that which the Divine Providence introduces.
That it is given to man to see the Divine Providence on the back, and not in the face; also in his spiritual, and not in his natural state. Explained. DP 189.
Without His Divine Providence, which is like a continual creation, could the infinite affections and derivative thoughts of men... be disposed so as to make a one...
That... the Divine Providence, from things most singular, is universal. General article. DP 201:2, Explained.
That the affections of the life's love are led by the Lord through His Divine Providence, and the thoughts at the same time, from which is human prudence. Explained.
That the Lord through His Divine Providence composes the affections into one form, which is the human one. Explained. This is a universal of the Divine Providence.
Providence with God is called prudence with man... So that we cannot speak of a universal Providence, if men provide all things from Own prudence.
(The universality of the Divine Providence in relation to creation.) Explained.
Of this universal Providence man sees nothing...
That those who have acknowledged God and His Divine Providence make Heaven. Explained.

Whence and what the Divine Providence is. - It is the Divine operation with the man who has removed the love of self... This being removed, the Lord enters with the affections of the love of the neighbour, and opens the windows... and makes him see that there is a Heaven, etc... and, through the spiritual light and the spiritual love then inflowing, makes him acknowledge that God, through His Divine Providence, rules all things.
Unless man, as from his own prudence, disposes all things of his function and life, he cannot be led and disposed from the Divine Providence. Explained.
Therefore if you want to be led by the Divine Providence, use prudence, as a servant and minister who faithfully dispenses the goods of his lord. Signified.
This is the prudence with which the Divine Providence acts as one.
The Divine Providence operates so occultly... lest man should perish. Explained.
The Divine Providence in ultimates... by constancies and inconstancies acts marvellously with human prudence; and at the same time hides itself.
That the Divine Providence regards eternal things, and temporal ones no otherwise than as they agree with eternal ones. General article.
That the conjunction of temporary and eternal things with man is the Lord's Divine Providence. Explained. DP 220:2. DP 220:4. DP 220:8.
That the Lord through His Divine Providence continually disposes that evil be by itself, and good by itself, so that they can be separated. Explained.
That the Lord through His Divine Providence most carefully provides that (truths) are not received by the will sooner or more than man as of himself removes evil in the external man. Explained.
That the laws of permission also are laws of the Divine Providence. General article.
He who does not acknowledge the Divine Providence at all, in his heart does not acknowledge God; but, instead of God, nature; and instead of the Divine Providence, human prudence.
By the tree of life is there meant the Lord as to His Divine Providence; and by the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, man as to Own prudence.
All the laws of the Divine Providence are necessities.
That the Divine Providence is equally with the evil as with the good. General article. DP 287.
That the Divine Providence with the evil is the continual permission of evil, to the end that there may be a continual withdrawal from it. Explained.
That the evil cannot be completely withdrawn from evils, and led into goods, so long as they believe Own intelligence to be everything, and the Divine Providence not anything. Explained.
That the Divine Providence continually causes man to see truth, and also gives the affection of perceiving and of receiving it. Explained.
This is done because the Divine Providence acts from the interior...

He who believes in the Divine Providence is withdrawn from evil; but he who does not believe in it, is not withdrawn; and he believes in it who acknowledges evil to be sin, and wills to be withdrawn from it...
That the Divine Providence does not appropriate evil to anyone, nor good to anyone... General article.
Under Prudence, see this reference.

That the Lord cannot act contrary to the laws of the Divine Providence; because to act contrary to them would be to act contrary to His Divine love and contrary to His Divine wisdom; thus contrary to Himself. General article.
Among the things which proceed from the Lord, the Divine Providence is primary...
The operation and progression of the end through the means is what is called the Divine Providence.
It may also be said that the Lord is Providence, as it is said that God is order; for the Divine Providence is the Divine order primarily concerned with the salvation of men...
That the operation of the Divine Providence to save man begins from his birth, and lasts to the end of his life, and afterwards to eternity. Explained.
That the operation of the Divine Providence is continually effected through means from pure mercy. Explained. DP 336. DP 337.
The Lord's Divine Providence that... Signified, Explained. AR 427. AR 686.
That all things in the Heavens and on earth... are ruled through His Divine Providence, and take place according to it. Signified. AR 950.
When a youth sees a virgin provided by the Lord, and a virgin a youth...
(Internal conjunctions are provided on earth for those who...)
That the Lord provides similitudes for those who long for love truly conjugial; and, that if they do not exist on earth, He provides them in the Heavens. (Explained.)
It is said as from fate, instinct, and dictate, but it is meant from the Divine Providence; because when this is not known it so appears. CL 316:3.
The Lord's most singular and thence most universal Divine Providence is concerned with and is in the marriages in the Heavens... CL 229.
The operation of uses through these spheres is the Divine Providence.
His government, which is called Providence, is carried on according to order...
Everyone ought to provide his body with food... and provide his mind with food...
The tenor of the Divine Providence as seen in my life. SE 3177.
On the Divine Providence. SE 1758. SE 2163. SE 2483. SE 2605. SE 2714. SE 3165. SE 4201.
On Foresight and Providence. SE 1885. SE 4704. DMin 4652.
All the objects which move man's thought... are of the Providence of the Lord, which can never be penetrated.
On Providence and influx. SE 4002. SE 4095.

On Providence and miracles. - Man can never be made better... if he obtains what he desires, and knows how everything is: all things ought to be contrary to his cupidities and thoughts; and still he should believe that the Lord rules everything. Explained.
On the Lord's Providence in the most singular things.
On Providence. - It acts calmly, and always draws upwards...
The government of the Lord's Providence is through affections; thus through good into truth.
On Providence and fate.
Presence and Providence. Signified, Explained.
For all the presence of the Lord is Providence.
The Divine Providence from His Divine love. Signified, Explained. AE 152.
The appearance in ultimates of the Divine guard and Providence as to wisdom. Signified, Explained.
The appearance in ultimates of the Divine guard and Providence as to intelligence, and as to clear view on every side. Signified, Explained. AE 284.
To receive... wisdom = the Divine Providence. Explained.
For the Divine good united to Divine truth proceeding from the Lord in the Third Heaven is received as the Divine Providence...
They heard a great voice = the Lord's Divine Providence.
Meanwhile provided with more. Signified. For that which is from man is prepared; but that which is from the Lord is provided.
Wonderful = from the Divine Providence.
The Laws of the Divine Providence. General articles. AE 1136:2. AE 1138. AE 1139. AE 1140. AE 1150:3. AE 1152:2. AE 1153:5. AE 1155:3. AE 1158:2. AE 1162:2. AE 1173:2. AE 1185:2. AE 1199.
2. The Divine wisdom is that which is called the Divine Providence... and Divine truths are what are called the laws of the Divine Providence...
Ship captains trust in the Divine Providence more than landsmen.
